title: Existing inlines and helpers are required; expanded bodies are rejected
summary: Expanded header asserts and hand-expanded header inline bodies must be mapped back to the existing inline/helper when line numbers and local evidence identify the source-level operation; keeping the expanded body is rejected.
Local helper boundaries must be restored when duplicated expanded bodies or sibling functions show an authored helper shape.
The hard lint for copied header inline bodies (copied_jobj_inline) runs on Melee C only; everywhere else duplicated_inline_body is a warning and the game's marker record governs hand-expanded bodies.
do: Use assert file and line numbers to find the owning header inline.
Use the existing header setter/getter helpers and local inline forms when they represent the operation.
Use a convenience accessor macro only when local evidence supports that access shape.
Restore local inline helper boundaries when sibling functions share the same body shape and objdiff supports the helper call or inline.
do_not: Keep an expanded header __assert(...) block when the header inline is identifiable.
Copy or paste header inline helper bodies into consuming TUs.
Duplicate a helper instead of calling the canonical header helper or adding the missing helper at the owning API layer.
Treat a convenience accessor macro as unconditional cleanup.
Redefine or manually expand header helpers to force a match without objdiff evidence.
Duplicate a local helper body into multiple wrappers when a shared inline helper represents the source shape.
preferred_repairs: Use header file/line evidence to recover the owning header helper or inline.
Use a convenience accessor macro only when local evidence supports that access shape.
Restore shared local helpers, such as quicksort-style wrapper bodies, instead of keeping duplicated expanded versions.
provenance: Melee header-helper and accessor-macro wording and examples moved to the Melee game slice (global_standard:melee-conventions); global text is game-neutral.

title: Project assert and report macros are required when they represent the source
summary: Raw assert/report expansions must become the project's assert, assert-with-message, assert-with-report, report, or panic macro forms whenever the file, line, message, and side effects match local project idioms; a shipped raw expansion that had a macro form is rejected.
There is no exception: an existing macro form must replace the raw expansion, and real report/panic side effects may not be dropped.
do: Use the project's plain assert macro for plain assertions.
Use the message- or report-bearing macro variant when message or report side effects are real.
Preserve real report and panic behavior while removing generated assert blocks.
do_not: Leave direct __assert blocks when an existing macro is the source-level form.
Invent fake assert strings, report globals, or dummy storage to force a match.
Drop a real report or panic side effect.
qa_enforcement: hard_lint; unrolled_assert lints Melee and sysdolphin .c only
preferred_repairs: Restore the project's assert/report/panic macro forms when they represent the source.
Preserve real report/panic side effects while removing raw assert expansions.
provenance: Melee assert-macro naming and examples moved to the Melee game slice (global_standard:melee-conventions); global text is game-neutral.
